payload.selection_rationale: Composed by the engine from E-001's design (design 219, made by SL-001 for the whole epic and attacked once, whole). This part builds: WHAT IT BUILDS: - internal/store/migrations/0002_reports.sql, run under the possession runner. - HBAND_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES in internal/config: `^[1-9][0-9]*$`, at most 209715200, default 26214400. - internal/reports: the Report library component, covering save by slug (create or replace), Publish, Unpublish, Delete, the queries, the package write mutex, and the Open sweep of tmp/* and orphan <id>.html files. - serveRaw in internal/server/raw.go, with the cache parameter. - The admin report rows in adminRoutes, with their templates: the GET /admin landing (list plus upload form with `<input type="file" name="file">`, title, slug and status published|draft), POST /admin/reports, GET /admin/reports/{slug}, GET /admin/reports/{slug}/raw (no-store, drafts included), and POST /admin/reports/{slug}/publish, /unpublish and /delete. TESTS: go test -count=1 ./internal/reports ./internal/server. Accepted: - A body of exactly cap. - UTF-8 BOM HTML, and HTML that starts with <meta>. - status=published sets published_at, and <data>/reports/<id>.html is byte-equal to the upload. - status=draft leaves published_at NULL. - Re-uploading an existing slug keeps the id and published_at, and swaps the bytes, sha256, size and title. This runs on this Windows PC. - Unpublish then republish keeps the original date. - Delete removes the row, and os.Stat reports the file gone. Refused, each leaving no row change, no file and an empty tmp/: - cap+1, which is 413; - two file parts; a .zip name; a .txt name; zip bytes or PNG bytes named x.html; a UTF-16 BOM file; - the slugs 'Bad Slug', '../x', '' and 81 characters; - an empty title; status 'live'. - A cross-origin POST gets 403. Deferred items owed here: - TestReplaceCommitFailureKeepsFileConsistent (m8): with an injected commit failure, the file bytes, sha256 and size still describe the old report, and tmp/ is empty. - TestDeletedIDNotReused (M-add-2): create, delete the newest, create again, and the new id is greater. - The preview response carries Cache-Control: no-store and the sandbox CSP in place of the site CSP (m4). Also: - Startup removes a planted tmp file and an orphan 999.html. - TestAdminAccessMatrix covers every new row with {slug}=x, with no edits. - No headless-Edge preview test: spike 193 is its evidence. FINISH LINES: SC-002 supplies the upload, replace, unpublish and delete halves of finish lines 1, 3, 4 and 5. Every finish line also opens /reports/<slug> or /raw, so lines 1 to 6 first pass once SC-005 has landed too.

components.name: Config loader (C-001)
components.responsibility:
`Load(getenv func(string) string) (Config, error)` validates every variable at once. It returns one error naming each bad variable and never echoes HBAND_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET.

REQUIRED:
- HBAND_OWNER_GITHUB_ID: exactly `^[1-9][0-9]{0,18}$`, and strconv.ParseInt(...,10,64) must succeed. Everything else is refused (lesson #103).
- HBAND_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID and HBAND_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET: non-empty.
- HBAND_BASE_URL: absolute, with https on any host or http only on 127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost. The path must be empty or '/', with no query, fragment or userinfo.

OPTIONAL:
- HBAND_ADDR: default 127.0.0.1:8080.
- HBAND_DATA_DIR: default ./data.
- HBAND_GITHUB_URL (default https://github.com) and HBAND_GITHUB_API_URL (default https://api.github.com): each held to the same URL rule as the base URL, with a trailing '/' trimmed.
- SC-002 adds HBAND_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES: `^[1-9][0-9]*$`, at most 209715200, default 26214400.

Load reads no other name. HBAND_TRUSTED_PROXIES, which the finish-line harness sets, is ignored and left for C-006 to decide.

DERIVED:
- Origin, and CallbackURL = Origin + /auth/github/callback.
- SecureCookies: on when the scheme is https.
- GitHub{AuthURL = GITHUB_URL + /login/oauth/authorize, TokenURL = GITHUB_URL + /login/oauth/access_token, UserURL = API_URL + /user}.
- GitHubOverridden: either endpoint differs from its default.

This is the only non-test file allowed to name the endpoint variables (architecture rule).
components.key_interactions: Called once by cmd/hband before the store opens or anything listens. In-package tests pass a map-backed getenv or build Config literals that point GitHub at fakegithub.

components.name: Entrypoint
components.responsibility:
`main()` is `os.Exit(realMain(ctx, os.Getenv, os.Stderr))`, with ctx from signal.NotifyContext. realMain:
1. Loads config. On error it prints every bad variable and returns 2.
2. Creates the data dir (0700) and opens the store at <data>/hband.db. Failure returns 1.
3. Builds server.New and listens on HBAND_ADDR. Failure returns 1.
4. Logs owner_github_id, base_url and the listening address. When GitHubOverridden is set it also logs a warning that names github_url and github_api_url.
5. Serves with ReadHeaderTimeout 10s and IdleTimeout 120s, and no global Read or Write timeout. The upload cap bounds uploads instead.
6. When ctx ends, runs Shutdown(10s), closes the DB and returns 0.

It never logs the secret, codes, state, tokens or cookie values.
components.key_interactions: cmd/hband/main_test.go runs realMain in-process for bad config. It also builds the real binary and drives it with the finish-line environment shape (lesson #754).

components.name: Store and migration runner (C-001)
components.responsibility:
`Open(path)` is `openWith(path, embeddedMigrations)`. openWith is unexported and takes an fs.FS, so tests can inject migrations.

MIGRATIONS run under POSSESSION, on a separate *sql.DB with SetMaxOpenConns(1) and one db.Conn:
1. Refuse if user_version is higher than the newest embedded migration.
2. For each pending NNNN_name.sql: PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF outside any transaction, BEGIN, the SQL, PRAGMA foreign_key_check (any row means ROLLBACK and an error naming the migration and the table), PRAGMA user_version=N, COMMIT.
3. A deferred PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON runs on every exit path.
4. The handle is closed.

Only then is the serving pool opened, with DSN `file:<path>?_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)&_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=foreign_keys(1)`.

SCHEMA 0001 (STRICT):
- users(github_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(github_id>0), login TEXT NOT NULL, avatar_url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL)
- sessions(token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY, github_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(github_id) ON DELETE CASCADE, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL), indexed on expires_at

Times are unix seconds. No column records owner, admin or role.

METHODS:
- `SignIn(ctx, SignInArgs{User, OldTokenHash (optional), NewTokenHash, ExpiresAt, Now})`: in ONE transaction, upserts the user, deletes expired sessions, deletes the incoming session and inserts the new one. It returns nil or an error with nothing written.
- LookupSession(hash, now), which joins users and counts only rows with expires_at > now.
- DeleteSession(hash), Ping, and DB() for internal/reports.
components.key_interactions: internal/auth calls SignIn, LookupSession and DeleteSession. SC-002 appends 0002_reports.sql, which runs under the same possession protocol.

components.name: Cookie and redirect helpers (C-002)
components.responsibility:
COOKIES. cookies.go is the only file that builds or writes a cookie.
- `setCookie(w, cfg, base, value, maxAge)` and `clearCookie(w, cfg, base)` always write HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax set explicitly, Path=/ and no Domain. When cfg.SecureCookies is on they add Secure and name the cookie '__Host-'+base. A clear uses the same attributes with an empty value and MaxAge -1.
- `cookieName(cfg, base)` is used for reading.
- Base names: hband_sid (Max-Age 2592000, persistent, which spike 193's Mode 2 depended on) and hband_oauth (Max-Age 600).

REDIRECTS. `LocalPath(s) (string, bool)` accepts s only if all of these hold:
- 1 to 512 bytes, every byte in 0x21..0x7E, so no tab, newline, space, DEL or raw non-ASCII;
- no backslash and no case-insensitive '%5c' anywhere;
- s[0] == '/', and s[1], when present, is neither '/' nor a backslash;
- url.Parse(s) gives an empty Scheme, Host and Opaque and a nil User.

Otherwise it returns ('/', false).

`SeeOther(w, target)` runs LocalPath and writes the accepted string verbatim with Header().Set("Location", ...) and WriteHeader(303). It is the only way any package answers a 303. Nothing in the repo calls http.Redirect (architecture rule), because its path.Clean would rewrite a validated value.
components.key_interactions: Used by the OAuth handlers, the session code, RequireOwner and every internal/server redirect. The login handler's 302 to GitHub is the one absolute redirect, written directly with Header().Set and WriteHeader(302).

components.name: GitHub OAuth flow (C-002)
components.responsibility:
GET /auth/github/login:
- Runs LocalPath on `next`, then mints a 32-byte state (43 base64url characters) and oauth2.GenerateVerifier().
- setCookie(hband_oauth, `<state>.<verifier>.<base64url(next)>`, 600).
- Answers 302 to AuthCodeURL(state, S256ChallengeOption) on cfg.GitHub.AuthURL, with RedirectURL = CallbackURL, no scopes and AuthStyleInParams.

GET /auth/github/callback is GET or HEAD only:
1. clearCookie(hband_oauth) on EVERY outcome.
2. The cookie must split into exactly 3 parts with a 43-character state, compared in constant time to the query state.
3. An `error` parameter or a missing code means 400, and the token endpoint is not called.
4. Exchange with VerifierOption and a 10 s client, which must return a non-empty AccessToken.
5. GET cfg.GitHub.UserURL with Bearer. `id` must be a raw JSON integer > 0 (json.RawMessage, then ParseInt), and `login` must be non-empty. Any failure is 502.
6. LocalPath on the decoded next.
7. store.SignIn. On error: 503 'Sign-in could not be saved, try again', with no hband_sid Set-Cookie.
8. Only after nil: setCookie(hband_sid), then SeeOther(next).

The access token is used once and dropped.

POST /auth/logout:
- DeleteSession(hash). On nil: clearCookie(hband_sid), then SeeOther('/').
- On a store error: 503 with no Set-Cookie, so the cookie and the row are both kept.
- With no valid session: SeeOther('/').
components.key_interactions: Uses cfg.GitHub (production: github.com, or an override validated by config), store.SignIn, an injected clock, cookies.go and SeeOther.

components.name: Sessions and Identify middleware (C-002)
components.responsibility:
Tokens are 32 crypto/rand bytes, base64url without padding (43 characters). The DB key is hex(sha256(token)). Sessions last 30 days absolute, with no sliding renewal and a new token at every sign-in.

Identify runs on every route:
- A hband_sid value that does not match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$` is anonymous, with no DB call.
- Otherwise it calls LookupSession and puts Viewer{GitHubID, Login, AvatarURL, IsOwner} in the context, with IsOwner = IsOwner(cfg.OwnerGitHubID, id).
- A store error is recorded as identifyErr. Public pages then render as anonymous and the gate denies.

`ViewerFrom(ctx)` is the read API for later blocks.
components.key_interactions: Wired between CrossOriginProtection and the mux. Read by RequireOwner, the home page, the reader header and later epics.

components.name: Owner gate (C-002)
components.responsibility:
`IsOwner(ownerID, githubID int64) bool` returns ownerID > 0 && githubID == ownerID. It is the only allow rule in the code, recomputed on every request from in-memory config.

`RequireOwner(h)` sets Cache-Control: no-store first, then:
- identifyErr: 503.
- Anonymous GET or HEAD: SeeOther('/auth/github/login?next=' + url.QueryEscape(r.URL.RequestURI())).
- Anonymous with any other method: 403.
- A non-owner: 403, on a page saying 'This GitHub account cannot open admin pages', with a sign-out form and no admin markup.
- The owner: puts Owner{GitHubID, Login} under a private context key and calls h.

`OwnerRoute(fn func(w, r, Owner)) http.Handler` is the second interlock: with no Owner proof in the context it answers 403 and never calls fn. `OwnerFrom(ctx)`.
components.key_interactions: Mounted twice by the router, on the exact /admin and on the /admin/ subtree, both wrapping the same adminMux. Every adminRoutes row is adapted through OwnerRoute.

components.name: HTTP server and router (C-001)
components.responsibility:
`New(cfg, store, clock) http.Handler`. The chain from outside in:
1. securityHeaders: the site CSP `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' https://avatars.githubusercontent.com; frame-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'`, plus nosniff and Referrer-Policy same-origin.
2. http.NewCrossOriginProtection() with AddTrustedOrigin(cfg.Origin).
3. auth.Identify.
4. The mux.

Admin wiring:
- `adminRoutes []adminRoute{Method, Pattern, Handler func(w, r, auth.Owner)}` is registered into adminMux by a loop, `adminMux.Handle(rt.Method+" "+rt.Pattern, auth.OwnerRoute(rt.Handler))`, so no /admin literal is ever passed to Handle.
- It is mounted exactly twice: `mux.Handle("/admin", auth.RequireOwner(adminMux))` and `mux.Handle("/admin/", auth.RequireOwner(adminMux))`.
- The exact /admin mount exists because the finish line requires GET /admin to answer 200 with no redirect.

Public routes: GET /{$}, the /auth/* routes, GET /static/ (embed), and GET /healthz (200 'ok', or 503 if Ping fails).

SC-001's home page shows 'Signed in as @login', a sign-out form and an Admin link for the owner. Every sign-in control on every page is `<a href="/auth/github/login?next=...">`, never a <form>, so form-action stays 'self'.

Scheme and host come only from cfg. No handler reads r.Host, r.TLS or the Host, Origin or Referer header, or any forwarded header.
components.key_interactions: Tests import adminRoutes, so every SC-002 row joins the access matrix with no test edits. Templates use html/template only.

components.name: Admin console (C-009)
components.responsibility:
SC-001 has two adminRoutes rows, GET /admin and GET /admin/{$}, served by one handler. It renders `<main data-hband-admin>` with '@login (owner)', the avatar and a POST /auth/logout form. data-hband-admin is the marker the tests check is absent from every refusal.

SC-002 rows:
- The same GET /admin row, now with the report list and the upload form: multipart POST /admin/reports with fields title, slug, status=published|draft and `<input type="file" name="file">`.
- POST /admin/reports: save by slug.
- GET /admin/reports/{slug}: the edit page. It frames `<iframe sandbox="allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox" referrerpolicy="no-referrer" src="/admin/reports/{slug}/raw">`, repeats the upload form with the slug filled in, and has publish, unpublish and delete forms.
- GET /admin/reports/{slug}/raw: serveRaw with drafts included and cache "no-store".
- POST /admin/reports/{slug}/publish, POST /admin/reports/{slug}/unpublish and POST /admin/reports/{slug}/delete.

Spike 193 measured that the Lax session cookie reaches that sandboxed frame. Cookie Path=/ makes the path shape irrelevant, so the preview stays behind the gate with no signed URL.
components.key_interactions: Handlers receive auth.Owner and call internal/reports. Every redirect goes through auth.SeeOther to a fixed local path.

components.name: Fake GitHub (test seam)
components.responsibility:
An httptest.Server bound to localhost, with three endpoints:
- /login/oauth/authorize: checks client_id, the exact redirect_uri, state and an S256 code_challenge, then 302s back with a single-use code.
- /login/oauth/access_token: checks the secret, code, redirect_uri and the S256 verifier. Like GitHub, it answers 200 with error=bad_verification_code on failure.
- /user: checks the Bearer token and returns {id, login, avatar_url}.

Switchable failures: DenyAtAuthorize, TokenError200, Token500, User401, UserMissingID, UserIDZero, UserIDString, UserIDFloat and UserEmptyLogin.
components.key_interactions: Imported only by _test.go files (existing rule). In-process tests point Config.GitHub at it. cmd/hband's TestBinary points HBAND_GITHUB_URL and HBAND_GITHUB_API_URL at it, which is allowed because it is a loopback http URL.

components.name: Report library (C-003, built by SC-002)
components.responsibility:
SCHEMA: `reports(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, title TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('draft','published')), published_at INTEGER NULL, size_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL, sha256 TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL) STRICT`, plus an index on (status, published_at, id).

RULES:
- Slug: `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`, 1 to 80 characters, and it is the report's admin key.
- Title: 1 to 200 characters after trimming, with no control characters.
- Status: exactly 'published' or 'draft'.

UPLOAD:
- Read with r.MultipartReader under http.MaxBytesReader(cap + 65536).
- Text parts are capped at 4096 bytes each. Unknown fields are discarded.
- Every part with a filename counts. There must be exactly one, its field name must be `file`, and its name must end in .html or .htm, case-insensitively.
- It streams into <data>/tmp/upload-<rand> while sha256 and size are computed. Size over cap means 413.
- Sniff: after removing one UTF-8 BOM, DetectContentType of the first 512 bytes must be text/html; charset=utf-8 or text/plain; charset=utf-8.
- Every refusal removes the tmp file before answering, and leaves no row.

SAVE (one package mutex around every write):
- New slug: insert the row (published_at = now if published, else NULL), rename the tmp file to reports/<id>.html, commit. If the commit fails, remove that file.
- Existing slug: update title, status, bytes, sha256 and size, with published_at = COALESCE(published_at, now) when the status is published and kept otherwise. Move reports/<id>.html to tmp/<id>.old, rename the new file into place, then commit. If the commit fails, restore the old file. After a successful commit, remove the .old file (m8).

ACTIONS:
- Publish: COALESCE the date.
- Unpublish: status draft, date kept.
- Delete: commit the row removal, then remove the file. A remove error is logged and the sweep catches it.

Open sweeps tmp/* and any reports/<n>.html that has no row.

QUERIES: Latest() (published, ORDER BY published_at DESC, id DESC), PublishedBySlug, BySlug and ListAll.
components.key_interactions: Called by the SC-002 admin handlers and by the SC-005 reader and raw handlers. Later votes and comments reference reports.id, which AUTOINCREMENT never reuses.

components.name: Raw serving and reader pages (C-004 / C-008; serveRaw built by SC-002, public routes by SC-005)
components.responsibility:
`serveRaw(w, r, report, file, cache string)` is the only code that writes report bytes. It uses Header().Set to replace the site CSP and the gate's headers, and sets:
- Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
- `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox; default-src 'none'; script-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; font-src data:; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors <cfg.Origin>`
- nosniff, Referrer-Policy no-referrer, CORP same-origin and ETag "<sha256>"
- Cache-Control from the `cache` argument: "no-cache" for public /raw and "no-store" for the gated preview (m4).

It then calls http.ServeContent and closes the file before returning.

SC-005 builds the public routes:
- GET /raw/{slug}: published reports only.
- GET /{$}: Latest(), or 200 'No reports yet'.
- GET /reports/{slug}: PublishedBySlug, with an identical 404 for anything unpublished.

Both pages render one template: the title, the publish date, the header with the anchor sign-in control, and `<iframe src="/raw/{slug}" sandbox="allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox" referrerpolicy="no-referrer" title="{title}">`. They never contain report bytes, and never name any report other than the one shown.
components.key_interactions: Framed by the reader page and the admin edit page with the same sandbox tokens. Later epics add the like count and comments under the iframe.

key_decisions.decision: Identity is the GitHub numeric user ID, the INTEGER PRIMARY KEY of users. The owner is whoever's ID equals HBAND_OWNER_GITHUB_ID, recomputed on every request by IsOwner(ownerID, githubID) = ownerID > 0 && githubID == ownerID. No role, owner or admin column exists.
key_decisions.rationale: This is the project constraint, and it is enforced by the existing rule 'being the owner is never stored in the database'. Logins can be renamed and reclaimed, which is why DevNotion [1] pins the numeric id. Recomputing per request revokes a previous owner at the next restart. Every later block keys on this ID.

key_decisions.decision:
The finish line overrides the attempt-1 endpoint lockdown. Config reads HBAND_GITHUB_URL (default https://github.com) and HBAND_GITHUB_API_URL (default https://api.github.com).
- Each must be https, or http on a loopback host. Path empty or '/', no query, fragment or userinfo. Anything else exits 2.
- Startup logs a warning naming both URLs whenever either is overridden.
- The other env names follow the tests too: HBAND_ADDR, and SC-002's HBAND_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES. HBAND_TRUSTED_PROXIES is ignored.

The SC-001 build deletes the rule entry 'the identity provider's endpoints cannot be set from the environment' from .taad/fitness.yaml. TAAD created that file, so changing it is TAAD's to do. This design appends the replacement, 'the identity provider's endpoints are read only by the config loader': the same pattern, with internal/config/config.go excepted.
key_decisions.rationale:
Every finish-line test sets HBAND_GITHUB_URL and HBAND_GITHUB_API_URL to its stand-in GitHub. Each one fails at its first sign-in unless /auth/github/login redirects to `<stand-in>/login/oauth/authorize`. A person approved those tests, so they outrank a design-time rule.

The rule's threat was 'a fake identity provider signs anyone in as the owner'. That needs control of the environment, and anyone with that control can already set HBAND_OWNER_GITHUB_ID to their own ID, so the override adds no privilege. What remains is an accidental leftover test override. The https-or-loopback rule refuses a remote http fake outright, and the startup warning makes an override visible.

The engine only appends rule names it has not seen. Leaving the old rule in place would fail config.go on every validate, so it is removed once, by name.

key_decisions.decision:
The owner gate stays structural, with two interlocks.
- RequireOwner wraps adminMux on exactly two mounts: the exact /admin and the /admin/ subtree.
- Admin handlers exist only as adminRoutes rows, registered by a loop through OwnerRoute.
- GET /admin is the admin landing page and answers 200 itself. GET /admin/{$} serves the same page.

The access matrix expects one outcome per ServeMux variant class:
- Cleaned (//admin/, /admin/../admin/, //admin): 301 to the clean path, for every identity and method.
- Case (/ADMIN, /ADMIN/): 404.
- Gated (/admin, /admin/, /%61dmin, /%61dmin/, /admin/%2e%2e/admin/, /admin/does-not-exist, and every adminRoutes path with {slug}=x): anonymous GET or HEAD gets 303 to login, other anonymous methods get 403, a non-owner gets 403, and the owner never gets 401, 403 or 503.

One invariant decides security: no anonymous or non-owner response is 2xx or carries data-hband-admin, and any Location is /admin, /admin/ or /auth/github/login?....
key_decisions.rationale:
The finish-line client never follows redirects and requires /admin to answer 200 with the upload form, so relying on ServeMux's 301 from /admin to /admin/ fails finish line 1. Both mounts are wrapped directly in auth.RequireOwner(, which the existing /admin registration rule allows.

M1 (accepted) showed that a single uniform status cannot hold across variants. A variant that misses both mounts can only get a 404 or a mux 301, because adminMux is referenced nowhere else. Per-class codes rest on recall: a builder may correct a class's expectation only by quoting the observed response, never by changing routing.

key_decisions.decision:
Sign-in navigation:
- Every sign-in control is an <a href="/auth/github/login?next=...">, and form-action stays 'self'.
- `next` is accepted only if LocalPath passes on the exact string that will be sent: printable ASCII, at most 512 bytes, no backslash, no %5c, one leading '/' not followed by '/' or a backslash, and url.Parse finds no scheme, host, opaque part or userinfo.
- SeeOther writes that string verbatim, and nothing calls http.Redirect.
- The gate's `next` is RequestURI, query-escaped.
key_decisions.rationale:
M-add-1 (accepted): http.Redirect's path.Clean turned `/./<backslash>evil.example` into `/<backslash>evil.example` after the check, and browsers follow that off the site. Validating the emitted string closes that class.

Refusing every byte outside 0x21..0x7E also closes the WHATWG tab and newline stripping that could turn `/<tab>/evil` into `//evil`.

m3 (accepted): Chromium applies form-action to the redirect chain after a form submission, so a sign-in form would be silently blocked on its 302 to github.com.

The %5c refusal is a belt-and-braces pin, and the first thing to trim. A verbatim %5C cannot change the host.

key_decisions.decision:
Cookies are built only by setCookie and clearCookie in internal/auth/cookies.go. Both always write HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax set explicitly, Path=/ and no Domain. On https they add Secure and the __Host- prefix, deletions included.

Session: a 32-byte token hashed with sha256 at rest, 30 days absolute, rotated at sign-in, persistent Max-Age. OAuth state, PKCE verifier and next travel in one 600 s Lax cookie, with no oauth_states table.
key_decisions.rationale:
m1 (accepted): a __Host- deletion that lacks Secure or Path=/ is silently ignored, and only in production. One constructor makes the attribute set a property of the code rather than of each call site, and the new rule forbids building cookies anywhere else.

Spike 193's Mode 2 depended on a persistent cookie. Spike 192 forbade Strict.

key_decisions.decision: The callback's store work is one transaction, store.SignIn. The session cookie is set only after it commits. Any SignIn error answers 503 with the OAuth cookie cleared and no session cookie. A failed DeleteSession at logout answers 503 and keeps the cookie.
key_decisions.rationale: m7 (accepted): this makes it impossible to hand out a cookie for a session that was never written, or to say 'signed out' while the row survives. One store call gives the handler one failure branch instead of four partial states.

M-add-3 (accepted): PRAGMA foreign_keys does nothing inside a transaction. With foreign keys on, SQLite's documented table rebuild cascade-deletes child rows: every session now, and every comment and vote later.

Crossdomain's separate handle was chosen over practice's dedicated Conn on the serving pool. No serving connection ever had foreign keys off, so the 'failed re-enable leaks into the pool' branch does not exist. Every later slice appends to this runner, so it can only be fixed here.

key_decisions.decision: Cross-site protection is http.CrossOriginProtection with AddTrustedOrigin(cfg.Origin), plus Lax cookies. There are no CSRF tokens. Unsafe-method requests that carry neither Sec-Fetch-Site nor Origin are let through, which is what the finish-line harness sends.
key_decisions.rationale:
This is the decided stack. The finish-line tests' admin POSTs carry neither header, and their form() helper tolerates a page with no CSRF token, so the decided mechanism and the tests agree. That rests on recalled CrossOriginProtection behaviour (outside_claims).

Spike 193 measured that Sec-Fetch-* is absent on plain http to non-loopback hosts. Config refuses that setup for the base URL, so browsers in production send Sec-Fetch-Site.

key_decisions.decision:
Reports (SC-002):
- An integer id (AUTOINCREMENT, never reused) and a unique slug that is the admin key.
- POST /admin/reports is save by slug: a new slug creates, an existing slug replaces. Replacing swaps the bytes and takes the submitted title and status. published_at is set once by COALESCE and never moved by replace, unpublish or republish.
- Actions are POST /admin/reports/{slug}/publish, /unpublish and /delete.
- Files live at <data>/reports/<id>.html. Replace sets the old file aside and restores it if the commit fails.
- The draft preview stays the gated row GET /admin/reports/{slug}/raw.
key_decisions.rationale:
The finish-line tests drive replace by uploading again under the same slug and expecting 2xx or 3xx. They post status=published|draft and act on /admin/reports/<slug>/<action>. The proposals' 409, id-keyed routes and action= field would fail finish lines 1, 3 and 4.

The report is the primary entity, and later votes and comments reference reports.id, so AUTOINCREMENT (M-add-2) cannot be added later without rebuilding the table. m8 keeps the file bytes, sha256 and size consistent.

Spike 193 measured YES for the Lax sid on the sandboxed preview frame, in both modes. Cookie Path=/ means the change from {id} to {slug} in the path does not affect it. There is no signed preview URL and no new data.

key_decisions.decision:
Report isolation (SC-005):
- Report bytes leave the server only through serveRaw.
- Its CSP is `sandbox allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox; default-src 'none'; script-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; font-src data:; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors <cfg.Origin>`.
- The iframe carries the same sandbox tokens, with no allow-scripts and no allow-same-origin.
- Everything is on one origin. The cache policy is a parameter: no-cache for public, no-store for the preview.
key_decisions.rationale:
This meets the isolation constraint without a second origin. It matches finish line 6's parser, which needs a sandbox without allow-scripts, unsafe-inline with no nonce or hash, and data: for images and fonts.

Spike 193 measured the request and its cookie under this CSP, not whether the frame renders under frame-ancestors plus sandbox. SC-005's headless-Edge test settles that. A failure there changes a header value, not a contract.

payload.coherence_check: One part of E-001, built against the design every other part of it is built against.

cases.behaviour: SC-002: WHAT IT BUILDS: - internal/store/migrations/0002_reports.sql, run under the possession runner. - HBAND_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES in internal/config: `^[1-9][0-9]*$`, at most 209715200, default 26214400. - internal/reports: the Report library component, covering save by slug (create or replace), Publish, Unpublish, Delete, the queries, the package write mutex, and the Open sweep of tmp/* and orphan <id>.html files. - serveRaw in internal/server/raw.go, with the cache parameter. - The admin report rows in adminRoutes, with their templates: the GET /admin landing (list plus upload form with `<input type="file" name="file">`, title, slug and status published|draft), POST /admin/reports, GET /admin/reports/{slug}, GET /admin/reports/{slug}/raw (no-store, drafts included), and POST /admin/reports/{slug}/publish, /unpublish and /delete. TESTS: go test -count=1 ./internal/reports ./internal/server. Accepted: - A body of exactly cap. - UTF-8 BOM HTML, and HTML that starts with <meta>. - status=published sets published_at, and <data>/reports/<id>.html is byte-equal to the upload. - status=draft leaves published_at NULL. - Re-uploading an existing slug keeps the id and published_at, and swaps the bytes, sha256, size and title. This runs on this Windows PC. - Unpublish then republish keeps the original date. - Delete removes the row, and os.Stat reports the file gone. Refused, each leaving no row change, no file and an empty tmp/: - cap+1, which is 413; - two file parts; a .zip name; a .txt name; zip bytes or PNG bytes named x.html; a UTF-16 BOM file; - the slugs 'Bad Slug', '../x', '' and 81 characters; - an empty title; status 'live'. - A cross-origin POST gets 403. Deferred items owed here: - TestReplaceCommitFailureKeepsFileConsistent (m8): with an injected commit failure, the file bytes, sha256 and size still describe the old report, and tmp/ is empty. - TestDeletedIDNotReused (M-add-2): create, delete the newest, create again, and the new id is greater. - The preview response carries Cache-Control: no-store and the sandbox CSP in place of the site CSP (m4). Also: - Startup removes a planted tmp file and an orphan 999.html. - TestAdminAccessMatrix covers every new row with {slug}=x, with no edits. - No headless-Edge preview test: spike 193 is its evidence. FINISH LINES: SC-002 supplies the upload, replace, unpublish and delete halves of finish lines 1, 3, 4 and 5. Every finish line also opens /reports/<slug> or /raw, so lines 1 to 6 first pass once SC-005 has landed too.

epic_part.title: Author uploads, replaces, unpublishes and deletes HTML reports from the admin pages
epic_part.description: From the admin page the author uploads a single self-contained .html file (images and styles embedded in it), gives it a title and slug, and publishes it now or saves it as a draft. Also, merged from SC-003 (Author replaces, unpublishes or deletes a report): Not built: `git ls-tree -r ba7102d` on uat lists no files. Replace under the same slug, unpublish and delete work on the same report record (C-003) and admin screen (C-009) that SC-002 creates, so one design covers the whole lifecycle and one review reads it, instead of a second full loop over code SC-002 just wrote. 'Likes and comments are kept' holds because replace keeps the report's identity, which SC-002's test pins; votes and comments themselves arrive with SC-010 and SC-011.
